stem:
Meera is helping her grandmother plant tulsi and mango saplings in their courtyard. She notices that their leaves are broad and flat. Her grandmother says this shape helps the leaves make food more efficiently.

Which statement best justifies why broad, flat leaves make photosynthesis more efficient?

options.text: A broad, flat shape gives a large surface to receive sunlight, so the green leaf can make more food at its main food-making site
A broad, flat shape makes the leaf heavier, so it can store more water for making food
A broad, flat shape helps the leaf take in more soil minerals directly from the air
A broad, flat shape stops sunlight from reaching the leaf, so the leaf does not dry out

teacher.key_rationale: Photosynthesis occurs mainly in leaves; a broad, flat lamina maximises the surface area exposed to sunlight, and the chlorophyll in the leaf uses this light to make food. Only option A connects leaf shape to sunlight capture and the leaf's role as the main food-making site. B confuses shape with water storage, C wrongly suggests minerals are absorbed from air, and D reverses the relationship by claiming the shape blocks sunlight.
